post.description: Checks the answer against the value sealed in the challenge. Each puzzle takes one answer (PUZZLE_MAX_ATTEMPTS) and its challenge string is then spent; the next response carries a fresh one. A person passes a group by answering PUZZLE_GROUP_CORRECT puzzles correctly (PUZZLE_GROUP_CORRECT_AUDIO in an audio group). A correct answer before that, or a wrong one within PUZZLE_GROUP_MAX_WRONG, returns the next puzzle of the group (`step` and `steps` count the progress); the answer that completes the group returns a token, and the wrong answer after PUZZLE_GROUP_MAX_WRONG wrong ones returns `retry` with a fresh challenge at PoW difficulty PUZZLE_POW_BUMP bits higher. A client that receives an unknown `type` MUST treat the answer as failed.

post.description: Verifies a response token. Server-to-server only. Every input, authentication or authorization failure (missing or invalid secret; missing, invalid, expired or duplicate response; sitekey mismatch; disabled site; quota; a browser request carrying an Origin header) is answered with HTTP 200 and `{ "success": false, "error-codes": [...] }`. A request carrying an Origin header gets `error-codes: ["bad-request"]` and no CORS headers. The only non-200 responses are 413 (body too large) and 5xx (internal error); clients MUST treat any non-200 as not verified. The secret is sent in the request body, or as `Authorization: Bearer`, never in the URL. A body in another media type, or with a non-identity `Content-Encoding`, is a malformed body: 200 with `bad-request`, never 415. Accepts application/x-www-form-urlencoded and application/json. (Server behaviour arrives in M1.) Firewall integrations send the secret as `Authorization: Bearer rgsk_...` instead of the body field `secret`; the secret is in exactly one of the two (both is `bad-request`). Unknown request fields are rejected (`bad-request`).

post.description: Server-to-server. A token assessment verifies a response token (one use, shared with siteverify) and returns its score and reasons; an express assessment (`event.express: true`) scores `event.userIpAddress` with no token. Body limit 8 KiB. JSON only; a query string or an Origin header is `bad-request`. `event.userInfo` is accepted as before and ignored when the site has neither account protection nor MFA on, and under `ACCOUNT_KILL`. Account verification (`accountVerification`) is off until the site enables it (`403 feature-disabled`). Payment fraud (`event.transactionData`, section 20) and SMS toll fraud (a phone number in `event.userInfo`, section 21) are each off until the site enables them (`403 feature-disabled`); `event.fraudPrevention: DISABLED` skips payment scoring. A card number, expiry, CVV or track data in `transactionData` is `bad-request`. Every other field not listed is rejected. The shadow score, the model, the fired rules and the rule, count or threshold behind a label are never returned.

userIpAddress.description: End-user IP address (IPv4 or IPv6). Express only.

accountId.description: Your account identifier: 1 to 256 UTF-8 bytes. Send this or `hashedAccountId`, never both.

hashedAccountId.description: A hash of your account identifier you computed: canonical padded standard base64 of exactly 32 bytes (44 characters). Send this or `accountId`, never both.

createAccountTime.description: When the account was created (RFC 3339). At most 600 seconds before now makes the assessment an account creation; otherwise it is a login.

userIds.description: Accepted for compatibility. Ignored, except that with the site's `smsTollFraud` flag on the first `phoneNumber` is scored for SMS toll fraud (section 21): it is used only in request memory, stored only as keyed hashes and never logged. Nothing else here is stored, hashed or logged.

phoneNumber.description: E.164. Accepted by the schema; answered `403 feature-disabled` until SMS is offered (section 17).

labels.description: Labels from an open enum: `PROFILE_MATCH`, `SUSPICIOUS_LOGIN_ACTIVITY`, `SUSPICIOUS_ACCOUNT_CREATION`, `RELATED_ACCOUNTS_NUMBER_HIGH` and `CREDENTIAL_STUFFING_SUSPECTED`. Clients MUST tolerate unknown labels. A label never comes with the rule, count or threshold behind it.

get.summary: Fetch the signed firewall policy bundle of a site
get.description: Public by site key, unless the owner marked the bundle private: then `Authorization: Bearer rgsk_...` (the site secret) is required and a missing or wrong one is `401 unauthorized`. Returns the bundle of section 18.5 as JSON with an `ETag`; a request with a matching `If-None-Match` gets 304. Cached for 60 seconds at the edge. The bundle is signed (Ed25519): integrations verify it against pinned keys and never trust the transport. An unknown or disabled site, and a site that has published no policy, are one `404 not-found`. Integrations that hold a secret send it on every fetch (section 18.5).

post.summary: Verify a response token (drop-in compatible path)
post.description: Verifies a response token. Server-to-server only. Every input, authentication or authorization failure (missing or invalid secret; missing, invalid, expired or duplicate response; sitekey mismatch; disabled site; quota; a browser request carrying an Origin header) is answered with HTTP 200 and `{ "success": false, "error-codes": [...] }`. A request carrying an Origin header gets `error-codes: ["bad-request"]` and no CORS headers. The only non-200 responses are 413 (body too large) and 5xx (internal error); clients MUST treat any non-200 as not verified. The secret is sent in the request body, or as `Authorization: Bearer`, never in the URL. A body in another media type, or with a non-identity `Content-Encoding`, is a malformed body: 200 with `bad-request`, never 415. Accepts application/x-www-form-urlencoded and application/json. (Server behaviour arrives in M1.) Firewall integrations send the secret as `Authorization: Bearer rgsk_...` instead of the body field `secret`; the secret is in exactly one of the two (both is `bad-request`). Unknown request fields (for example `version` from existing server libraries) are ignored.

response.description: The response token: 1 to 2048 characters of unpadded base64url (`A-Z a-z 0-9 - _`).

remoteip.description: End-user IP address (IPv4 or IPv6). An invalid value is ignored, not rejected.
